topics: Greatest Common Divisor Euclid’s and Extended Euclid’s Algorithm for GCD
Prime numbers and Prime Factorisation - Primitive Roots
Existence of Primitive Roots for Primes
Principles of security - Types of Security attacks
Symmetric key Ciphers - Block Cipher principles & Algorithms- DES, AES

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks.  Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.  Each question can have a maximum of 3 subdivisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Explain the integer arithmetic operations including divisibility and GCD algorithms, modular arithmetic operations and properties, polynomial arithmetic, and algebraic structures such as groups, rings, and fields.
Describe the number theory concepts essential for cryptographic applications and mathematical problem-solving.
Explain the security principles, types of attacks, and protective measures, alongside a thorough understanding of cryptographic techniques and their applications in securing data.
Discuss  symmetric and asymmetric key cryptography, including block cipher principles, algorithms, public key cryptosystems, and hash functions
